correctness.rationale: Every finite word has exactly one restricted-growth representative of its letter-equality partition; Parikh-border equality and the number of used letters survive relabeling. Exhaustive generation of all Bell(11)=678570 such representatives and all shorter lengths with two distinct border-array routines produces the exact minimum-rank table. A separately implemented Python complete enumeration reproduces all 11 rows and the C++ program checks every witness. The persistence theorem is a direct prefix argument. The proof is finite and exhaustive for n<=11, not extrapolated from sampled words.

value.rationale: The primary 2021 paper explicitly singles out larger-alphabet realizability as substantially harder than binary and offers only partition upper bounds. The minimal alphabet required by a complete prefix-border array is a canonical reconstruction invariant. This result determines the first three higher-alphabet transition points sharply (4,8,11), all first-appearance fibers, and the complete natural initial rank table rather than selecting a single arbitrary instance. The persistence implication guarantees genuine rank-five distinctions for every greater word length. No claim is made about a closed formula at arbitrary n.
